extra.reason: Fixed in 3d0c508: from_json_bytes now runs the same simd-json parser as from_json_str/from_json_bytes_mut; the public serde Deserialize impl decodes the arbitrary_precision number token (const-parameter visitor mode, zero-cost on the simd path). Success-path + literal-magic-key + round-trip tests added. All gates green (conformance 1733/1733, clippy 121, fmt, wasm).

Fixed in 7dedd84: scan_regex consumes a backslash plus the full UTF-8 char it escapes as pattern text, so escaped brackets never move the depth counter (subsumes the old even/odd close-slash walk). docs/spec.md 2.5 updated, including a documented bidirectional deviation from jsonata-js on brackets preceded by an even number of backslashes (parity semantics chosen: /\\(x)/ lexes here, /\\}/ is S0302). 17 conformance cases + 6 lexer unit tests. Gates green (1750/1750, clippy 121).

Fixed in e6b387d: removed eval_chain's undefined short-circuit — every ~> stage now applies unconditionally, matching jsonata-js evaluateApplyExpression. Verified against a 45-expression jsonata-js matrix (all match post-fix; e.g. filter->count gives 0, substringAfter->exists gives false, undefined-propagating signatures still propagate). 13 conformance cases added, 9 of which fail on the old code. Gates green (1763/1763, clippy 121).

Fixed in daa49b5: mark_tail_position no longer sets thunk on a Function node carrying a group-by, so eval_group_by can never receive a TailCall sentinel. Note: reference jsonata-js is itself buggy here (drops the group, and leaks its own lambda sentinel for parenthesized callees), so the fix matches jsntrs's own non-tail semantics ({"k":{"v":1}}), which equal jsonata-js's non-tail semantics. 4 conformance cases + unit test. Gates green (1767/1767, clippy 121).

Fixed in 6129dab: collect_path_steps hoists a group-by found on any dot node in a flattened chain onto the resulting Path (S0210 if the chain carries more than one), matching jsonata-js processAST: a.b{G}.c behaves as (a.b.c){G}. Verified against jsonata-js on 10 expression/data variants (incl. arrays, chained groups, parenthesized forms). 9 conformance cases. Gates green (1776/1776, clippy 121).

Fixed in d85e80b: the array-constructor unwrap in fast_path::try_function is now restricted to //// via unwraps_array_constructor(kind), with the -deferral subtlety documented (([])=0 vs (undefined)=undefined is safe only because the Sum arm defers to the original AST on zero leaves). 32 differential divergences before, 0 after; 16 jsonata-js-verified expectations pinned in testdata. Gates green (1792/1792, clippy 121).

Fixed in dc6b434: fast_path::try_function now requires keep_array:false, group:None on the Function node, so $sum(prices)[] and $sum(prices){"k":$} fall through to the general path, mirroring collect_pure_path guards. 34 differential divergences before, 0 after; group-by shape pinned in testdata (jsonata-js-verified). The [] shape is deliberately NOT pinned in conformance: the general path itself diverges from jsonata-js there (filed as a follow-up). Gates green (1799/1799, clippy 121).

Fixed in 38c6905: extract_param_field now takes the Path node and mirrors fast_path::collect_pure_path (rejects keep_singleton_array on the Path and keep_array on the Name); three duplicate analyzer helpers collapsed into it so every lifted shape (FieldAccess, predicates, sort/reduce, concat templates, mapped-call args) shares one guarded predicate. 36 differential divergences before, 0 after; 9 jsonata-js-verified conformance cases. Gates green (1808/1808, clippy 121).

Fixed in 0dc1590: analyze_mapped_call declines the lift when the resolved callee is a Lambda declaring more params than the call supplies, deferring to the general paths (path steps prepend the context item, lambda-body calls pad with undefined — the arg template cannot distinguish them). Differential cases added (LAMBDA_ARITY fixtures); fail-before: 8 divergences. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in 869bc43: new is_mirrorable_literal gates the reversed literal-op-field normalization in analyze_binary and collect_predicate_clauses — only Number/String literals may move right (always pass compare left-operand type check); Eq/Ne stay unrestricted (symmetric). Fast path now matches general/jsonata-js T2010 on null/boolean vs missing field. +7 conformance cases (rust-hof-compare-literals), differential cases added; fail-before: 16 divergences. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in a46e487: MappedCall carries a check_signature flag (set when the general path would run eval_function: block-wrapped step or lambda-body call); exec_mapped_call replays process_call_args for SignedBuiltin callees before call_function. Deliberately NOT applied to bare function path steps whose general path (eval_path_function_step) performs no validation — unconditional checking would create the mirror divergence. +7 conformance cases (rust-hof-signature-lift), differential cases; fail-before: 16 divergences + 4 conformance failures. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in f06f595: new fast_path::eval_fast_with_bindings serves only binding-free fast-path classes (PurePath, Comparison) and the env-carrying entry points (evaluate_with_env, evaluate_with_custom_funcs, evaluate_with_vars, StreamEvaluator batch env) route through it; the Function class (26 FuncFastKind names) now takes the general path under caller bindings, honouring overrides. jsonata-js verified: binding shadows builtin (99), assign wins (77), non-function binding raises T1006 — all matched and pinned. Existing $round pin test kept (covers the dx5.13 prepared-state gate); new $sum tests cover each entry point. Measured cost confined to env-carrying func-fastpath expressions; follow-up filed for canonical-identity restoration. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in c44c5cc: the issue premise (keepArray never read on bare Function nodes) was WRONG — jsonata-js reads it generically but guards with isSequence(result). Plain deletion would have regressed flattening/case044 and function-match/case002. Implemented the real rule: call [] applies only when the result stands in for a sequence — stdlib::returns_sequence identity-matches the four builtins jsonata-js builds with createSequence but jsntrs collapses ($keys/$lookup/$filter/$match) via canonical Rc tables; Lambda => false so tail and non-tail agree. Same fix applied to the ~> chain step. Full verification matrix (bare/path-step/parens/lambda) matches reference; +24 conformance cases (rust-keep-array-call), 2 differential cases; fail-before: 13 conformance failures + 4 divergences. Gates green, clippy 121.

Resolved in 091c740 (tests only, jointly with jsntrs-e8l/c44c5cc): after e8l a lambda callee never honours [], so the direct path and the trampoline agree in every position — the tail/non-tail split ($id(5)[] vs tail $id($n)[]) is gone by construction. Pinned with +10 conformance cases (rust-keep-array-tailcall) and a position-independence unit test; fail-before evidence captured against the pre-e8l epilogue. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 24b83fc): eval_tuple_group now applies the reference key rule regardless of tuple mode — non-string non-undefined key raises T1003, undefined key skips the item, result starts as {} and is returned as-is (all-undefined group yields {} in both modes). Verified against jsonata-js source (evaluateGroupExpression) and a 35-expression matrix, 35/35 match post-fix. +15 conformance cases (rust-tuple-group-key); fail-before: 11 conformance failures with T1003. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 1c86579): $sift and $each now route callback dispatch through hof_args (args trimmed to callee declared arity; builtins get value only, matching the $map/$filter convention and jsonata-js getFunctionArity which uses implementation.length), and $each supplies the object as 3rd arg. hof_args takes a lazy second-arg closure so the key/index allocation stays off the arity-0/1 path — perf-neutral in a same-session A/B. docs/spec.md 5.5.8 corrected (Go-reference deviation labeled). +24 conformance cases (rust-hof-arity) + 2 unit tests; fail-before: 9 conformance failures. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked dcfd382): extract_comments tracks a closed flag and no longer slices src[start..i] when a /* is never closed — format("/*\u{20AC}") now returns the lexer S0106 instead of panicking. Same change fixed an adjacent latent bug: regex literals containing escaped /* no longer emit a dangling comment. Byte-index audit recorded in the doc comment (ASCII delimiters cannot match UTF-8 continuation bytes). 5 unit tests added; new fuzz target fuzz_format (panic-freedom of format and format∘format) ran 1.27M execs clean; build verified on main post-pick. Fuzzer surfaced 4 pre-existing formatter round-trip bugs, documented in the target header — filing as follow-up beads. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 98d1857): finiteness guard at $formatInteger entry raises D3001 "Number out of range" (same code/idiom as $string on Inf/NaN, per spec.md), stopping the float_to_words infinite loop; debug_assert added in float_to_words. Reachability wider than filed: 1/0 propagates Inf from plain JSON expressions, so the +6 conformance cases (rust-format-integer-nonfinite) pin it with pure fixtures; unit test crosses 13 pictures x Inf/-Inf/NaN = 39 D3001s. jsonata-js itself crashes (RangeError) or emits junk here, so a clean coded error is deliberately better than reference. Fail-before: hard hangs (exit 124/143) on w-pictures, "zero" for NaN. Gates green, clippy 121.

All three children fixed and closed: 5lw.1 (daa49b5, no thunk on grouped tail calls), 5lw.3 (6129dab, mid-path group hoist), 5lw.2 (091c740 with jsntrs-e8l/c44c5cc, call [] applies only to sequence results so tail and non-tail agree by construction). Thunk semantics decided: decorated nodes either are not thunked (group) or the decoration is a no-op for lambda results ([]).

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked ecc3b2d): FmtChars::from_opts parses exponent-separator; field widened to Option<char> (single char = Some, empty/multi-char = None so NO picture char is an exponent separator — mirrors jsonata-js char-vs-string matching where multi-char can never match, avoiding a value-vs-error divergence). Default e correctly becomes INACTIVE when a custom separator is set (D3086, matching reference). Unknown option keys stay ignored, matching jsonata-js — pinned. +15 conformance cases (rust-format-number-exponent), all expectations from reference; fail-before: 14/15 fail. Gates green, clippy 121. Reference bugs jsntrs does not share (prefix+exponent D3093, hang on negative/zero exponent pictures) documented in notes; one real jsntrs divergence (exponent separator treated as active in prefix/suffix scan) filed separately.

Done in HEAD (cherry-picked f07abb7): the differential harness now PROVES a lift fired — fast_path::testing gained a cfg-gated hit counter (zero-cost in release/wasm) bumped at the five sites the disable flag guards; assert_fast_matches_full asserts hits>0 and panics on bad fixtures; new assert_declined_matches_full asserts hits==0. CASES split into lift-required (250 pairs) and GENERAL_ONLY_CASES (180 pairs), enforced both directions — 144 vacuous pairs flushed and re-tiered, none deleted. New coverage: the 4 uncovered FuncFastKinds (Values/Reverse/Shuffle/Flatten), aggregate array-arg matrix completed, 19 missing kinds under []/{} postfix, 10 remaining reversed-literal combos + $sort/$reduce hosts, and an evaluate_with_env lane on every pair (empty custom env must never change an answer; override behavior owned by named unit tests, documented in header). Also fixed a real coverage bug: parenthesised $reduce accumulators never exercised ReduceCompoundAccum — unparenthesised twins added. Genuine divergence found and excluded (extends jsntrs-6wr.9, issue updated). Gates green, clippy 121, fuzz build ok.

Fixed in HEAD: cargo update rand (0.9.2 -> 0.9.5, dev-only via proptest) and bench/engines/js jsonata ^2.1.0 -> ^2.2.2 (lock resolves 2.2.2, >= 2.2.0 fixes the $toMillis DoS). Full gates green (conformance 1916/1916, clippy 121). Bench-engine version bump noted for the pending re-baseline. Both Dependabot alerts should auto-close on scan.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked db9cbd1): derived the rule from jsonata.js source — evaluate() wraps every node so sequences collapse before reaching any syntactic position; jsntrs evaluates lazily, so a new eval_operand (eval + collapse_sequence_in_place) now runs at every consumer boundary (call args, binary operands, unary, constructor items/keys, subscript index/predicate, sort keys, transform update/delete, ~> stages). Two deliberate non-collapse sites mirror apply() running outside evaluate(): raw builtin callback results embed as plain arrays in HOFs, and tail-call lambda bodies return raw (new Lambda::tail_call_body, computed to match reference tail positions — deliberately NOT copying our mark_tail_calls Bind arm, which looks like a latent bug, filed). $keys/$lookup/$filter/$match now return real Value::Sequence, subsuming and DELETING the e8l CANONICAL_SEQUENCE tables; both e8l residual corners fixed. All headline repros now match reference ($count($map)=2, $map(items,$keys)=[["a"],["b"]], etc.); 105-case battery went 42 mismatches -> 1. The 1: $distinct sequence-flag deviation kept (flagged; matching it would re-open the leak — follow-up filed). p0v.10 nested-$each repro RESOLVED by this fix. +44 conformance cases (rust-sequence-args, all reference-generated), 17+13 differential pairs, no existing expectation changed. Perf: interleaved min-of-K A/B shows ~3% on subscript/aggregation-heavy shapes, rest in noise — the price of 1-3 discriminant compares per operand. Gates green, clippy 121, fuzz builds.

Resolved by the jsntrs-p0v.6 sequence-boundary fix (db9cbd1, integrated as a0b9b94): the nested $each single-item inner result no longer over-collapses. Verified on main post-integration: $each({"x":{"p":1}}, function($v,$k){ $each($v, function($val,$key){ $k & "." & $key }) }) now returns ["x.p"], matching jsonata-js. Pinned by the rust-sequence-args conformance group ($each callback-sequence cases).

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 1350d0b): eval_path_function_step was the only call site skipping process_call_args for SignedBuiltin callees; it now runs the same gate eval_function does (after the lambda context-prepend, which is mutually exclusive with SignedBuiltin). check_signature flag on MappedCall removed — validation is now unconditional, contract comment updated. Reference: applyInner calls validateArguments on EVERY invocation, no bare-step exemption; 29-row matrix verified, error codes and values identical (T0410 surplus args, T0412, nil propagation, singleton coercion all match). +27 conformance cases (rust-step-signature); 10 new bare-step differential pairs in CASES; fail-before: 10 conformance failures. Gates green post-merge with the p0v.6 sequence work, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 4a644f9): (1) the lift — analyze_mapped_call requires group: None on the Function node and extract_param_field requires group: None on the Path, so a {...} postfix always falls to the general path; all seven formerly-excluded header expressions moved into GENERAL_ONLY_CASES and the Known-divergence header section is gone. (2) the general path — eval_group_by now implements the reference rule read from evaluateGroupExpression: non-array base becomes a sequence, empty base pushes undefined, undefined KEY skips the item, defined key with undefined VALUE drops only the pair, and the (possibly empty) object is always returned — items.($string(x){k:$}) now yields [{k:3},{k:s},{}]. 60+ expressions reference-verified. Deliberate deviations documented in spec.md 4.12.1: jsonata-js TCO drops the group (and can leak a raw lambda object) — jsntrs applies it consistently (wave-1 5lw.1 decision); empty tuple-stream group crashes jsonata-js with a raw TypeError — jsntrs returns undefined. +37 conformance cases (rust-group-undefined-value); fail-before: 23 conformance failures + 27 tier divergences. Gates green, clippy 121. Epic 6wr now 9/9.

All nine children fixed and closed across three waves: 6wr.1-.3 (P0 wave: array-arg unwrap, postfix drops, keep_array guards), 6wr.4-.7 (P1 wave: custom-env gating, lambda arity, literal flips, signature validation), 6wr.8 (capstone: hit-count-enforced two-tier differential harness, 144 vacuous pairs flushed), 6wr.9 (group postfix bail + reference group semantics). The harness now proves every lift fires or is deliberately declined; fast-vs-general agreement is pinned by 250 lift-required and 200+ general-only pairs.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 44e31b9): process.rs::wrap_decorated_name promotes a lone Name to a single-step Path ONLY when it carries [] (and no group) or a focus/index binding — a bare Name is byte-for-byte unchanged (size_of Expr stays 144). Expr::Block gained keep_array so (…)[] on a path step hoists via step_has_keep_array; top-level block [] stays inert, preserving the pinned ($sum(prices))[] -> 60 boundary. Three reference-verified narrowings documented (name with []+group not wrapped; subscript LHS never wrapped — first draft broke flattening/case038; group stays on the Name step). ~110-pair reference matrix went 31 diffs -> 3; a[] -> [1], items.($string(x[])) -> ["[1]","[5]"], foo.($sum(bar))[] -> [3]. One accepted divergence, same class as pre-existing: x.(a[]) -> [1] vs ref 1 (eager materialisation in block steps — follow-up filed). +26 conformance cases (rust-lone-name-keeparray); fail-before evidence in track notes. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 8026cfd): wrap_decorated_name extended to a lone Name carrying an @$v focus or #$i index binding, so the path tuple machinery binds the variable — books@$b{$b.g:$b.t} -> {"a":"t1"}, books#$i{...} -> {"0":"t1","1":"t2"}, plus the ungrouped books@$b / books#$i / books@$b[] forms, all reference-verified. The #$i variant of the same hole was checked and fixed too. rust-tuple-group-key stays green. +21 conformance cases (rust-lone-name-focus). Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 2b8be7f): Expr::Regex::flags holds effective flags (lexer appends a synthetic g); new source_regex_flags() strips the single trailing g so format prints only source-writable flags — /abc/i round-trips instead of emitting /abc/ig (S0302 on re-parse; S0201 in jsonata-js). Two existing test expectations updated WITH proof they pinned the bug (regex_literals asserted the unusable /test/ig output). Conformance cases pin the lexer contract (rust-formatter-roundtrip). Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked df0d439): emit_lambda no longer wraps Signature::raw (which already includes the outer angle brackets) in a second pair — function($x)<n:n>{$x} round-trips instead of emitting <<n:n>> (S0402 on re-parse). Tests cover plain, nested/higher-order (<f<n:n>:n>), multi-arg, - and (sao)? forms, each asserted verbatim + re-parsed + idempotent + type-checked. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 287940f): escape_name replaced by name_spelling() — quoted when the name holds no backtick, BARE when it does (backtick quoting has no escape syntax; jsonata-js lexes a`b as one name and jsntrs matches), with the bare form verified by running the real lexer over it. Names with no spelling at all (unreachable from today parser) error via a new Formatter::error channel instead of emitting garbage. Both fuzz repros fixed (0x00 0x60 unterminated name; the non-idempotent statement-split case). Fuzzer re-parse + idempotence assertions ENABLED with 4 newly-found gaps fenced and documented in the target header (3.3M execs clean) — follow-ups being filed. Gates green, clippy 121, fuzz builds.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 0bf59c5): finiteness guard in $formatNumber raises D3001 (the ecq.3/$formatInteger/$string precedent — jsonata-js has no usable reference here, it emits NaN.00 junk), placed after T0410 type checks and undefined propagation so error precedence is unchanged (pinned). ALSO fixed the same divergence in the hof_fast mapped-call lift, which re-implements the builtin and would have kept formatting Inf while the general path raised D3001 (pinned by a hof_fast unit test; unreachable from JSON-fed differential lanes). +8 conformance cases (rust-format-number-nonfinite); fail-before: 7 failures with inf.00/NaN.00/(inf.0)/NaN%. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 2d87496): the exponent separator is excluded from the active-char test that locates a sub-picture prefix/suffix (matching jsonata-js ch !== exponent-separator) while staying active for splitting and output; new locate_exponent reproduces the reference rule that a separator at the start of the suffix introduces an (empty) exponent part -> D3093. "e0.0" -> "e1234.6", "0.0e" -> D3093, existing rust-format-number-exponent group stays green. Drive-by anti-panic guard: decimal-separator == exponent-separator produced an inverted slice range and a hard panic — now D3085 (was a panic on plain user input, invariant violation). +15 conformance cases (rust-format-number-exponent-scan), two pinning jsntrs answers where jsonata-js crashes or mis-splits (flagged, not silent). Fail-before: 11 failures + 1 suite panic. Adjacent D3093 gaps filed as follow-ups. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 6c124c1): mirrored the reference mechanism read from jsonata.js — processAST binary { (group-by) is the only construct that never calls pushAncestry, so % in a group pair is permanently unbound and evaluates to undefined (the undefined-key rule then yields {}). jsntrs group-by pair evaluation now runs in a frame binding %%=undefined, compositional so a % reached through a step INSIDE the pair still resolves. 15-row reference matrix matches including tuple-path variants and nested groups; S0217 still fires where genuine (%, $.%, chained %). DEVIATION from docs/spec.md 4.12.1 Go delegation sentence flagged (doc bead to follow). +15 conformance cases (rust-group-key-parent); fail-before: 11 failures. Gates green, clippy 121.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked edb09ed): every CLI failure path in jsntrs-bench now prints one clean stderr line and exits nonzero (compile error: S0201: ..., evaluation error: ..., input JSON error: ..., cannot read FILE, invalid -n) instead of panicking with Debug output — and a malformed -data payload is now a hard error instead of silently evaluating against undefined (bench scripts only pass generated fixtures, unaffected). Manually verified before/after on 9 failure shapes + happy paths; clippy also run with --features bench-bin (bin is behind required-features), still 121. Gates green.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 8f2873b): accepted like the reference. from_json_bytes/from_json_str retry through serde_json (public Deserialize, arbitrary_precision hands numbers as raw text to parse_number_token) ONLY on the simd-json Err arm — oversized ints widen to nearest f64, 1e400 becomes Infinity (write_json emits null, matching JSON.stringify). from_json_bytes_mut stays STRICT deliberately (simd-json rewrites the caller buffer in place — original document unrecoverable; documented + pinned). eval_tape_path now returns Option so a rejected document falls through to the Value route; record_hit moved after successful tape parse. Value::from_json fixed (as_f64 filtered non-finite -> NaN). BOM/tape errors get a clean message instead of InternalError(TapeError). +6 conformance cases (rust-json-number-limits, reference-checked incl. D1001/D3001 interactions), 5 differential pairs, 5 unit tests. A/B on parse benches: no systematic effect above the noise floor (untouched control row moved with the candidate); happy path adds zero work. Gates green, clippy 121, fuzz builds.

Fixed in HEAD (cherry-picked 3e6fbbe): the closure_envs suspect list (conservative Rc-cycle candidates, cleared by teardown_cycles at the API boundary) now sweeps amortized — when the list hits a threshold re-armed at 2x the surviving length, freed environments and repeat registrations are dropped, so it stays proportional to genuinely-retained scopes instead of one entry per lambda evaluation. Measured impact was NOT 8 bytes/entry: a stale Weak pins the whole ~146-byte RcBox — dhat on a 100k-lambda expression shows peak heap -64.7% (22.6MB -> 8.0MB), live blocks 100,201 -> 257, no leak either way. Rejected alternatives documented (bind-time detection misses container cycles; scope-exit clearing is unsound — closure escape does not raise the env strong count; Drop-based free list adds glue to the per-call hot path). Pinned CPU-time A/B on lambda-heavy shapes: +0.0% across the board. 3 new unit tests incl. the no-regression leak guard; fail-before: list grew to 5001/10000 in the bounded tests. Gates green, clippy 121. Real per-iteration scope retention bug found and filed separately.

Fixed in 823eeb0 on main. Root cause: scan_sub_picture_region exempted percent/per-mille inside the active picture region, so "0,%." passed validation, parse_int_part recorded a grouping separator with no digits to its right as grouping position 0, and compute_int_group_positions looped forever advancing by zero (the 58.5GB OOM of 2026-08-14). Fix: (1) any passive char inside the active region is now D3086, matching jsonata-js 2.1.0 (verified for "0,%.", "0,‰.", "#,%.", "0%0", "0‰0", custom percent chars; 0 over-rejections in a 13,112-picture adversarial sweep incl. exhaustive len<=4 and 18 option maps); (2) compute_int_group_positions refuses a zero primary — the repeating expansion is now total regardless of what parsing produces. Verified: trigger now errors in <1ms under a 2GB cap; hof_fast path covered (shares parse_sub_picture). Gates: lib tests +2 (interior-passive matrix incl. custom-percent regression, grouping totality), conformance 2120 -> 2126 strict (new group rust-format-number-passive, all jsonata-js-verified), clippy exactly 121, fmt clean. Behavioral diff over the 1600-case ndedges tsv: 108 lines changed, 65 now match reference, 20 error-CODE regressions on doubly-invalid pictures (D3086 shadows D3087-93; reference is last-checked-rule-wins) — deliberate first-error deviation documented in code and handed to jsntrs-p0v.23 with the full evidence. Follow-up bugs filed from the adversarial review: jsntrs-p0v.26 (negative-zero sign), jsntrs-p0v.27 (multi-char per-mille/pattern-separator options).

Integrated as 7b3191f (wave-5 track A; cherry-picked independently of by0/09h/a1e, which are parked). A transform now type-checks its document argument the way its <(oa):o> signature does: a scalar document raises T0410 instead of being returned unchanged, while objects and arrays of objects keep working. Verified by hand: x.(a[]) ~> |$|{'z':1}| on {"x":{"a":1}} and 5 ~> |$|{'z':1}| both T0410; $ ~> |$|{'z':1}| and $ ~> |a|{'z':1}| unchanged. 25 cases; conformance 2750 -> 2775, clippy 123, fmt clean. Re-verifier raised no blocking or concern finding against this commit. KNOWN GAP left open (filed separately): the check covers argument 1's TYPE but not the signature's ARITY, so an extra argument is still accepted. NOTE: an array of NON-objects is deliberately not an error — jsonata-js leaks a raw JS TypeError there, which is a bug we do not port.

Resolved as a convention, not a mechanism (user call): a case edited away from jsonata-js carries a free-text divergence note giving the reason and the spec citation. Documented in testdata/NOTICE and CLAUDE.md; commit d8e42d5. No harness change — the loader already ignores unknown fields, and grep finds the set.

Decided (user, 2026-08-15): the cast STAYS. The docs are silent on the digit count but not on the kind — their own published examples are rounded (13 sig digits, byte-exact toPrecision(13)), and the JSON.stringify sentence cannot bear an exact-output reading because two of the four casting bullets require a replacer. 15 is the live consensus count. jsntrs-1uk, jsntrs-wvq, jsntrs-p0v.24 all stand; jsntrs-x0y confirmed by the docs. Full evidence in notes. Follow-on work is jsntrs-nyn (unify the scalar path onto the cast), authorized in the same ruling.

Fixed in f6e8247. format_float now applies string_cast_number then renders with ryu-js — the same two steps the container arm takes — so $string(x) and $string([x]) can no longer disagree. Retired format_g15, scientific_to_decimal, clean_exponent and the Go 'g' pipeline; kept the non-finite 'null' spelling (six error-payload sites depend on it). Replaced format_small_band_keeps_full_precision (it pinned the wrong answer) with a band test and an arms-agree test. Added testdata/groups/rust-string-small-scalars: 57 cases, 19 values x scalar/array/&, every expectation recorded from jsonata 2.2.2 — all passed first run. rust-number-formatting/case000 corrected: $string(0.0000005) is '5e-7' (ECMAScript and the reference agree), not the Go pipeline's '0.0000005'. EXPECTED_CASE_TOTAL 2775 -> 2832. Gates: cargo test exit 0 / 0 failed, conformance 2832 strict, clippy grep 123 (unchanged), fmt clean.

Fixed across f0ad326, 5e2aaee, 16891e5 (wave 6 Track T, spec-derived from docs.jsonata.org). (b) $split rejects a non-string first argument — the docs say the first argument 'must be a string' — T0410 instead of silently coercing. Fixed in a94a917. docs/behaviors.md error catalog re-derived from docs.jsonata.org rather than from the implementation; new section 2.0 records what the documentation actually specifies about the error object. Verifier confirmed the quotes verbatim.

Fixed in d25b498 (wave 6 Track N). The $formatNumber output stage re-derived from XPath 3.1 F&O 4.7.4/4.7.5 instead of ported bullet-for-bullet from jsonata-js. Three of the four quirks docs/spec.md 5.2.20 called 'replicated deliberately' were JS artifacts and are gone: (a) bullet 12 removes the decimal SEPARATOR, not whatever character is last, so $formatNumber(1234.5678,'#e0') is '0.1e4' not '0.e4' — W3C QT3 numberformat231/232 confirm; (c) an integer grouping position past the number is SKIPPED, not wrapped through String.slice, so $formatNumber(7,'#,###,#') is '7' not ',,7' — QT3 numberformat320; (d) fractional grouping scans the part it was handed, so $formatNumber(1234.5678,'0.0,0,0') is '1234.5,6,8' not '1234.5,68' — QT3 numberformat157/158. Quirk (b), the both-minima-zero rule, turned out to be genuine 4.7.4 spec text and was KEPT, with the section now cited instead of being called a quirk. Verifier independently fetched F&O by curl (WebFetch truncates the 2.6MB page), confirmed all quotes verbatim, pulled the QT3 suite, and checked that the fixes GENERALIZE: 23 QT3-derived probes pass including six the track never added as cases, plus all four of F&O 4.7.4's own worked examples. Case total 2835 -> 2841.

Fixed in f582912 (wave 6 Track N). minus-sign is an F&O 4.7.1 decimal-format property and jsntrs was not reading it; 4.7.4 writes it into the negative prefix and 4.7.5 emits it. Also documents in docs/spec.md 5.2.20 that an empty, multi-character, duplicated or digit-family option value is not a legal decimal format under 4.7.1 ('a single character', 'distinct values', 'none of these properties may be equal to any character in the decimal digit family'), so jsntrs's behavior there records what it does rather than what the spec requires. infinity and NaN stay unread: both are unreachable, non-finite input being D3001. Case total 2841 -> 2844.

Fixed in 3cee459 (wave 6 Track N, filed and fixed in the same wave). Regular grouping is now decided by F&O 4.7.4's third condition — 'Every position in the integer part of the sub-picture that is a multiple of the grouping-separator position is occupied by a grouping-separator character' — rather than the previous approximation. 5 cases added; total 2844 -> 2849.

Fixed in ada0ad9 (wave 6 Track N). F&O 4.7.5 says the mantissa is converted to an xs:decimal and, among numerically equal candidates, 'the one that is chosen should be one with the smallest possible number of digits' — that is the shortest round-tripping decimal, the same digit sequence ECMAScript Number::toString produces. jsntrs was printing the double's exact binary expansion instead. Fixes numbers >= 1e21 and, as the verifier established, ordinary half-way rounding with them: $formatNumber(2.675,'0.00') was '2.67' and is now '2.68', $formatNumber(1.115,'0.00') was '1.11' and is now '1.12' (the exact doubles are 2.67499999999999982... and 1.11499999999999999..., so the old answers came from the binary expansion, not from 4.7.5's shortest decimal followed by round-half-to-even). Those two were unpinned; I added case047 to the output group so the choice cannot be silently reverted. $string and $round are unaffected — value/format.rs is untouched. Case total 2849 -> 2855.

Fixed in d372235 (wave 6 Track V). A fractional array subscript now rounds DOWN (f64::floor) rather than towards zero, at all four consumption sites. The documentation states the rule twice, and the verifier confirmed both quotes verbatim against the raw markdown sources. 26 cases added; total 2855 -> 2881.

Fixed in a052337 (wave 6 Track V, with an integration repair). select_by_indices now builds a Sequence and collapses it, so a one-element index-list selection yields the value rather than a one-element array: [1,2,3][[0]] is 1, and [1,2,3][[0]] = 1 is now true (CLAUDE.md invariant 2). The docs' own filter section calls that selection a 'result sequence', and rule 2 of sequence flattening collapses a singleton — so the old [1] genuinely violated the stated rule.
INTEGRATION REPAIR: the track's commit let an undefined escape into user-visible output. With a missing LHS and the [] flag, a[[0]][] on {} answered [undefined] — visible as $count 1, $exists true, {"k": a[[0]][]} growing a k the documentation says it must not have, and $sum throwing T0412 where the expression used to answer nothing. Root cause: the all-numeric branch called select_by_indices(from_ref(left)) without checking left.is_undefined(), and Sequence::with_items does not drop Undefined the way Sequence::append does; without [] the unwrap masked it. I added the guard before the branch and testdata/groups/rust-subscript-index-list/case041.json pinning seven of the verifier's repro rows. The verifier also noted the surface is wider than one line: 5[[1,2]] -> undefined, "x"[[0]] -> "x", {}[[0]] -> {}, $string([1,2,3][[0]]) -> "1" all changed too, and all now agree with the singleton-equivalence sentence. Case total 2881 -> 2928.

Fixed in 45cf47f (wave 6 Track V). Unary minus rejects a non-numeric operand: NaN takes the existing D1002 branch, a non-finite operand D1001. Note the verifier's caveat, recorded honestly: the documentation names no error codes at all and the NaN question is genuinely unaddressed (JSON cannot express NaN), so the codes chosen are jsntrs's own pre-existing assignments for those conditions rather than spec-derived — defensible, but not a spec citation. 15 cases; total 2928 -> 2943.

Fixed in 1af882a (wave 6 Track V). Fixed in 4942ef2 (wave 7 Track N, after wave 6 diagnosed it and withheld the commit). Fixed in 0779c54 (wave 7 Track N, user ruling). Fixed in 70c0399 (wave 7 Track F). dot_needs_padding now decides from the PRINTED TEXT of the following step rather than its node discriminant, which is what the idempotence gap was: format(format(x)) could differ from format(x) because the node kind and the rendered text disagreed about whether a joining dot needed padding. Closed as a FINDING, not a code change, in eb53e15 (wave 7 Track F). format() does not drop the decoration — Parser::set_focus/set_index/set_keep_array drop it before format() ever runs, so a numeric path step reaches the formatter already stripped. The formatter is printing faithfully what the AST holds. Fixing it means changing what the parser records, which is out of a formatter track's scope and needs its own issue if wanted; the commit documents the mechanism and where it lives.

Closed as a FINDING, not a code change, in fddcf62 (wave 7 Track F). Slot order is not represented in the AST at all: a#$i@$v and a@$v#$i parse to the same node, so the formatter cannot reproduce source order because the information is gone by then. The commit records that the printed order is canonical and means the same thing, which makes the round-trip AST-identical even though it is not byte-identical — which is what the round-trip invariant actually requires.

Fixed in 37948ff (wave 7 Track K), after two parked rounds in wave 5. A group-by pair whose value expression selected nothing is now DROPPED, with or without []. processing.md's sequence rule 1 is explicit and the third sentence is the load-bearing one the wave-6 derivation doc had omitted: 'If it is associated with an object property (key/value) pair in a result object, then that object will not have that property.' So a{'k': c[]} on {"a":[{"b":1}]} is {} where jsntrs answered {"k":[]}. A pair value that matched an EMPTY ARRAY FROM THE INPUT is unaffected — a{'k': c[]} on {"a":{"c":[]}} is still {"k":[]} in both engines, which is the distinction the old parking note got wrong. Its premise ('keep-array on an empty sequence is [], a defined value') was contradicted by the documentation, exactly as wave 6 predicted. apply_keep_array lost its undefined-replacement parameter (one call site). 7 cases; total 2980 -> 2987.

Fixed in 83fc6a7 (wave 7 Track K), after two parked rounds in wave 5. Two halves. (1) A sort stage re-orders its input and changes nothing else, so a one-value result collapses: a^(b) on {"a":[{"b":1}]} is {"b":1}, not [{"b":1}], and $count(a^($)) on {"a":[[3,1,2]]} is 3, not 1. The Sort stage 'sorts (re-orders) the input sequence' and rule 2 makes a singleton sequence equivalent to its value. A one-value result is returned as an UN-COLLAPSED Sequence so a following [] still has a singleton to keep. (2) A [] written on a step before a sort survives the sort and the stage after it — a[]^(b)[0] is [{"b":1}] and a[]^(b).b is [1] — because both keep-array walkers stopped at the Path node inside a Sort operand. 18 expression shapes over 10 documents moved. 19 cases; total 2987 -> 3006. INTEGRATION NOTE: the verifier objected that case017/case018 (a^($) and a^(b)[] on {"a":[]}) pinned an UNRESOLVED question — the reference answers undefined there, and by0's own citation chain arguably implies undefined. I kept the cases for regression detection but added divergence notes saying so, and filed jsntrs-jys to decide it.

Fixed in 168db5a (wave 7 Track K), after two parked rounds in wave 5. A sort whose terms mention % now keeps its operand's [] like any other sort: a[]^(%.k) on {"a":{"b":1},"k":2} is [{"b":1}], the same as a[]^(b). There is ONE Sort stage in the documented path-processing table, with no clause about what the sort key mentions, so the parent-tracking branch cannot mean something different — it was rebuilding the sequence from tuple contexts and never seeing the flag. Both branches now read the flag off the operand's Path node and return a one-value result un-collapsed, so a^(%.k)[] also keeps a matched array wrapped. The commit also fixes collect_tuple_results, which collapsed the tuple stream BEFORE flagging it and so lost the difference between a one-member sequence holding an array and an array of that many values: a.b[], a#$i.b[], a[].b#$i and a.b#$i[] now all agree, where jsonata-js is self-inconsistent across those four (it answers [[7,8]] for three and [7,8] for the fourth). 14 cases; total 3006 -> 3020. FOLLOW-UP FILED: jsntrs-dow, for the operands the % gate still does not recognise.

Fixed in 04233d5 (wave 7 Track K; filed and closed together, found while working jsntrs-09h). build_sort_ctxs bound the parent only for a Path operand, but an undecorated 'a' parses as a bare Name, so a^(%.k) raised S0217 — and only when the document had two or more values to compare, since the error came from inside the comparator, which made a documented STATIC error depend on input cardinality. Now a^(%.k), a[b>0]^(%.k) and *^(%.k) resolve % against the input, while function calls, array constructors and blocks still raise S0217 per the % page's navigation qualifier. 142 sweep rows moved from S0217 to a value, including Phone^(%.Age) on the repo's own dataset1.json. 5 cases; total 3020 -> 3025. Residual gaps tracked as jsntrs-dow.

Fixed in 1732e0c (wave 7 Track P). A new check_parent_context pass in parser/process.rs rejects at COMPILE TIME every % that does not navigate, which is what the documentation requires and the only error code it makes a language rule: 'It is implemented by static analysis of the expression at compile time ... If, for any reason, the parent location cannot be determined, then a static error (S0217) is thrown.' So 'false ? % : 1' is now rejected at compile time instead of evaluating to 1. The pass's design rule is that any position whose status is unclear is treated as NAVIGATING — an under-refusal only leaves today's evaluation-time S0217 in place, while an over-refusal would reject an expression that evaluates perfectly well.
VERIFICATION: the verifier reproduced the attribution independently rather than trusting the sweep — 54,498 rows across the merge base, this commit, and the branch head; 2,502 outcomes changed and every one was accounted for. A 360-row over-refusal grid (10 %-bearing fragments x 36 enclosing contexts) found no expression newly rejected that used to evaluate.
KNOWN GAP, filed as jsntrs-e9y: the Apply arm (PATH ~> $f(%)) falls into the generic Binary arm and inherits navigating=false, so a.b ~> $string(%) is rejected at compile time where jsonata-js answers a value — and the % page's own 'navigates through that target parent value in the first place' arguably favours the reference, since a.b does navigate. Not a regression (the merge base already raised S0217, just later), but it contradicts the pass's stated design rule. 18 cases; total 3025 -> 3043.

Fixed in the amended a4ec449 (wave 7 Track P). '..' is now recognised only between two elements of an array constructor, by the '[' prefix parser, rather than being an ordinary infix operator anywhere. docs.jsonata.org/numeric-operators: 'The sequence generator can only be used within an array constructor []'. So '1..5', '(1..5)', '$sum(1..5)' and 'a[1..3]' are now syntax errors (a predicate is the filter operator, not the array constructor), while '[1..5]', '[1..3, 5..6]', 'a[[1..3]]', 'a.[1..3]' and '[1+1..2*3]' all keep working. A precedence bug fell out with it: '[1 ? 2 : 3..4]' answered [2] because '..' bound looser than '?', and now answers [2,3,4].
TWO INTEGRATION FIXES. (1) The verifier showed case index 4, '[(1..3)]' -> S0202, is NOT entailed by the quoted sentence — it IS within an array constructor, and the extra rule about nesting inside a block is undocumented. Kept the pin with a divergence note saying it is unresolved, and filed jsntrs-2rp. (2) Cross-track collision with Track F: the formatter test for jsntrs-y3t used '0 . 2..3', which stops parsing once '..' leaves the general grammar. Replaced it with '0 . [2..3]', which turned out to assert something better — the printed text starts with '[' so the dot needs no padding and welds to '0.[2..3]', exercising the printed-text-not-node-kind rule in the direction the old node-kind test could never get right. 12 cases; total 3054 -> 3066.

Fixed in 0cadb75 (wave 7 Track P). The block loop ends at the first expression not followed by ';' and then requires ')', so '(1 2)' is a syntax error instead of being silently accepted. docs.jsonata.org/composition: 'Used to support code blocks - multiple expressions, separated by semicolons (expr1; expr2; expr3)'. Code choice noted by the verifier and accepted: S0202 is not documented for this, but it is already jsntrs's 'expected X got Y' code in the same '[' and '(' handlers, and it matches the reference. 11 cases; total 3043 -> 3054.

Fixed in 09c56cf (wave 7 Track P). A new filter_tuple_ctxs in evaluator/path.rs applies the documented filter rule to a parent step — a numeric predicate selects by POSITION, not by truthiness. Verifier sweep: 1,100 rows (25 predicates x 11 shapes x 4 documents), three-way; 304 outcomes changed, 304 moved ONTO jsonata 2.2.2, zero moved off, zero landed on something neither engine says. 12 cases; total 3066 -> 3078. DISCLOSED and accepted: group-by after a parent filter that now selects nothing gives undefined where it used to give a value (12 rows on a 336-row grid) — a consequence of the filter working, not a separate defect.

Fixed in 2b253e0 (wave 7 Track P). A new check_placeholder_position pass rejects a stray ? at compile time with S0211, and it runs BEFORE the parent check, so '(%).?' — invalid twice over — reports the ?, matching the reference, and '1.?' reports S0211 rather than the evaluation-time S0213 it used to reach. That ordering is the substance of the issue. The documentation gives ? exactly one role, the omitted argument of a partial application; jsntrs parsed one wherever a value could stand, so '?', 'a.?', 'a[?]', '[?]' all answered silently and "? & 'z'" answered 'z'. Code choice flagged by the verifier and accepted: S0211 is undocumented for this, but it is already jsntrs's code for a token that cannot open an expression, and it matches the reference. 14 cases; total 3078 -> 3092. KNOWN GAP, filed as jsntrs-ck4 and now qualified in docs/spec.md: the pass does not walk group-by pairs on a function invocation, so $string(1){'k': ?} is still accepted. The rest of the issue had no support above jsonata-js and was deliberately left alone.

Closed by efede9d (wave 7 Track P) as RESOLVED BY jsntrs-8kn plus documentation. The new compile-time check_parent_context pass (1732e0c) subsumes the % -inside-a-block case this issue was about: a % in a block step that does not navigate is now an S0217 at compile time, which is what the documentation requires. The commit records the step-kind rule the % definition gives and why the residue is not coded. NOTE the wave-5 history that made this issue expensive: its round 2 fixed all four round-1 items and introduced three new families, 71 hard acceptance regressions — the static pass reaches it from a different direction, and the verifier attributed 54,498 sweep rows to confirm nothing else moved.

Closed by efede9d (wave 7 Track P) as documentation. Done in 7b9416a (wave 7 Track H, redone by hand at integration). flag_keep_array took the Undefined substitute as a parameter and all four call sites passed Value::Undefined — which is exactly what mark_keep_singleton's own Undefined arm does, so the wrapper was pure indirection. Done in 7f43d29 (wave 7 Track H). Removed dead surface left from the port: FunctionValue::Partial (never constructed), the Stage/StageKind types and the Expr::Name 'stages' field (never populated — jsntrs models a predicate as an enclosing Binary(Subscript), which process.rs already documented), and the D3137_FLOAT sentinel code and Value::check_numeric (zero callers, and it disagreed with the live sites on NaN).

Vendored. testdata/oracles/qt3/ now holds format-number.jsonl (253 single-call cases), format-number-excluded.jsonl (16 held back, with the reason), the extractor script, a README with provenance, and LICENSE.md. $match now yields the documented {match, index, groups}; start/end removed. Three inherited cases migrated with divergence notes. a^($) on {"a":[]} now answers undefined, per the user decision. rust-sort-sequence case017/018 re-derived and their unresolved notes dropped. Plain 'a' on {"a":[]} still answers [] in both engines, as required.

S0202 kept for [(1..3)], per the user decision, and the licensing rule now stated in docs/spec.md: the sequence generator must be an ELEMENT of the array constructor, not an expression nested inside one, and a block is not an array constructor. Recorded honestly as jsntrs's reading of a rule the documentation implies but does not state. The unresolved note on rust-range-array-constructor case 4 is dropped; the case stays as a regression pin.

Won't-fix with a deviation note, per the user decision. docs/spec.md records it beside the 4.7.3 note, covering both halves of the same root cause ($distinct reading sequence-ness inside a builtin, and the lambda argument/return boundary). The documented contract says $distinct returns an array, which is what jsntrs answers; the reference's collapse to a scalar is a sequence-representation artifact leaking through a builtin.

Resolved on measurement: one of the two reported divergences was already gone (the wave-7 by0/09h fixes brought a[]^(<$)[-1] to [5], matching the reference), and the survivor is a reference defect, not a jsntrs one — /predicate says the [] flag belongs to the path ('the [] can be placed either side of the predicates and on any step in the path expression') and a Sort stage only re-orders, so $[]^(<$)[-1] is [5]. jsonata-js drops the flag there through an inconsistency in its own processAST lifting. Both shapes pinned.

Landed as 9db0385. The transform now routes through check_signature, so a second argument is T0410 on argument 2 rather than being silently ignored.
